testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air to brake several times if the compressor breaks.
Hold air only in an emergency.
Hold air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air to brake several times if the compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air so you can brake several times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Remove water and compressor oil from the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and compressor oil from the tank.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil that builds up in the tank. You should drain the tanks at the end of each day to prevent damage.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking up.
Stop the vehicle from speeding up on hills.
Stop the vehicle from speeding up going downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent the wheels from locking when you brake hard.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?
questions.explanation: Use the parking brake every time you park your vehicle.

questions.question: What do vehicles with dual air brake systems need before driving?

options.text: Full air pressure even when the engine is off.
Some air pressure when the engine is off.
Time for the compressor to build air pressure before driving.
No time to build air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Time for the compressor to build air pressure before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving, you must let the compressor build at least 100 psi of air pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: When should you test the low pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: Test your low pressure warning light before every trip. After the system charges, push and release the brake pedal quickly to release air. The light should come on when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: How fast do air brakes work after you press the pedal?
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is a delay of about half a second between when you press the pedal and when the brakes start working.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check the alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: In cold weather, check and fill the alcohol evaporator every day. It helps prevent ice from building up in the air brake system.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the yellow brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the yellow brake control knob.
questions.explanation: Pull the yellow diamond-shaped knob to set the parking brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: Where should the front brake limiting valve be set?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, keep it set to normal. The valve has a slippery setting, but it is not effective and should not be used.

questions.question: Brakes may get out of adjustment if:
questions.explanation: Brakes can lose adjustment quickly if they overheat from heavy use. Check your brake adjustment often.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times can:

options.text: Release air faster than the system can replace it.
Add more air to the brake system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than the system can replace it.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times removes air faster than the compressor can add it back.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Sends air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks. The governor controls the compressor.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in very wet weather when temperatures are below freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle will not move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle will not move.
questions.explanation: Using the parking brake in wet, freezing weather can cause the brakes to freeze. This will prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum air loss for a triple combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: Know the maximum safe air loss for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system works on different axles.

questions.question: To use the stab braking method in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Push the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until they roll again, then repeat.
Push the brakes about halfway and keep the wheels rolling.
Push the brakes fully, lock the wheels, and keep holding until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brakes fully until the wheels lock, release until they roll again, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking means fully applying the brakes until they lock. Then release them until the wheels start rolling again. Repeat this process.

questions.question: A modulating control valve controls:
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver slowly apply spring brakes. In vehicles with this system, the valve is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: When using the controlled braking method in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Push the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Push the brakes with about half your usual force.
Push the brakes so the wheels lock.
Push the brakes with minimal pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pushing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep steering movements small when braking this way.

questions.question: What can happen if air pressure is too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes may be slow to respond.
The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.explanation: If you pump the brake pedal too many times, air escapes faster than the compressor can replace it. If air pressure gets too low, the brakes will fail.

questions.question: The air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes is ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: The maximum allowed air leakage for a single vehicle with air brakes is 2 psi per minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: When only the tractor is equipped with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: There is a decreased risk of jackknifing.
There is an increased risk of jackknifing.
The brakes will not work as effectively as they would without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a decreased risk of jackknifing.
questions.explanation: When only the tractor has ABS and the trailer does not, the risk of jackknifing decreases. The driver can maintain better steering control. If only the trailer has ABS, it is less likely to swing to one side.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are equipped with:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.
